lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 16, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

Is Alex currently in approved education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or an equivalent full-time course) or training (such as a traineeship or foundation apprenticeship that is unpaid)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually just left school recently. He's signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next - you know, get some guidance on his options for college or work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. That's helpful to know.

Just to clarify - is the careers service Alex has registered with a **government-sponsored careers service** (such as the National Careers Service in England, Careers Wales, Skills Development Scotland, or similar official services)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - it's the National Careers Service here in England. He registered with them not too long ago after finishing school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming.

Now, I have a few more questions about your circumstances:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're here in England. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions:

1. Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
2. Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more a week, or started receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. And no, he's not working or receiving any benefits himself - he's just been focusing on sorting out his next steps with the careers service.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**For Alex (age 16):**
- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex lives with you, so you are responsible for him
- ✅ Alex has registered with a government-sponsored careers service (the National Careers Service)
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- ✅ He is not working 24+ hours per week or receiving benefits in his own right

**Important to note:** Because Alex is 16, has left education, and has registered with the National Careers Service, you can claim Child Benefit for him for **up to 20 weeks** while he uses the service to explore his options. If Alex decides to return to approved education or training during that time, you may be able to continue receiving Child Benefit beyond those 20 weeks.

If you haven't already been receiving Child Benefit for Alex, you would need to make a new claim. If you were already receiving it, you should ensure you notify the Child Benefit Office of his change in circumstances.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
